We only build where the return is clear. Every build starts with a bottleneck, a clearly defined goal and KPIs that prove its value.

No. We handle the technical side from start to finish. Everything we build fits into the tools you already use. Your team can change it without touching code, and we end with a documented handover and training.

# AI Consultant & AI Consulting in Denmark | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/ai-consultant/

AI consultant

# An AI consultant that builds what it recommends.

 An AI consultant looks at how your business runs, finds where AI can take work off your team and tells you what to build first. We do that, and then we build it. You get a ranked roadmap, a working system and a team that knows how to run it.

 01, What it is

## AI consulting in plain words.

 An AI consultant reviews how your business works, measures where the time goes and judges which steps AI can take over. The result is a ranked list of what is worth building, what is not and what each item can return. It starts with the work, not with a tool.

 Talk to us about this

### The work it removes

Guessing which AI tool to buy, trying things that go nowhere and reading advice that does not fit your business.

### What you get

A prioritised roadmap: what to build first, what comes after it and the return to expect at each step. We call this an AI audit.

### For example

Say your sales team spends the morning copying orders from email into the system, and quotes go out two days late. We follow one order from inbox to invoice and mark every manual step. The roadmap puts order entry first, because it takes the most hours, and quoting second.

 02, After the advice

## Advice is only half the job.

 Many AI consultancy firms hand over a report and leave. We stay for the build. The same people who found the problem set up the fix, so nothing is lost between the plan and the finished work. Read how that works on our AI implementation page.

 Talk to us about this

### What you skip

Hiring one firm to advise and another to build, and explaining everything twice.

### What we deliver

A working AI agent or automation, set up on accounts your business owns, with a documented handover and training so your team can change it without code.

### From plan to running

The roadmap says order entry goes first. We build an automation that reads each incoming order, checks it against your records, enters it and flags anything odd for a person to review.

 03, Tools

## Built with tools you can own.

 We pick the tool that fits the job. See what we build on our AI agents and AI automation pages.

 Talk to us about this

### Automation

n8n, Zapier and Make move data between your systems and run the steps in the right order.

### AI models

Claude and GPT read emails, documents and messages, write drafts and sort what comes in.

### Follow-up and contact

HighLevel, ManyChat and Instantly handle follow-up, chat and outreach. We also work inside your own systems, so nothing has to be replaced.

 04, Who it is for

## Made for owner-led and mid-size businesses.

 We work with businesses of about 10 to 500 staff, in Denmark and abroad. We have helped more than 100 businesses on six continents. You can see everything we offer on our services page.

 Talk to us about this

### A good fit

Repeat tasks eat hours of your team’s week, and nobody has time to test AI tools or work out which ones matter.

### Where we are

Mugisha AI is based in Copenhagen and works with businesses in Denmark and abroad.

### What we need from you

A person who knows how the work runs today and can answer our questions. We handle the technical side.

 05, AI audit

## What an AI audit covers.

 An AI audit is the first step of our AI consulting services: a review of how the work actually runs, not a list of tools. We follow one case from the first enquiry to the last step and note where tasks repeat, where data is typed in by hand and where work waits. The result is a ranked roadmap with the number the first solution should move, and a note of what is not worth building. What an audit covers point by point, how to prepare and how to judge a report are in our plain guide to AI audits.

### AI consultant, in-house hire or doing it yourself: when each fits

 This comparison is our own view, and we have an interest in the answer.

Option | Fits when | Watch out for | 

An external AI consultant | You want to know what is worth building, have one or a few clear tasks and no technical person with time for them. The same people give you the plan and the first build. | You are buying a defined piece of work, not a permanent colleague. Choose a consultant who also builds, or you end up with a report and no solution. | 

An in-house hire | The AI work is continuous and big enough for a full position, and you can attract and keep a person with those skills. | The role needs tasks from the first day, and one person is a weak point if they leave. | 

Doing it yourselves with the tools you have | The task is small and clear, it is a single process, and someone on the team has both the time and the appetite to try things out. | The time comes out of other work, and attempts can stall between a trial and daily use. Write down how the solution works so it does not depend on one person. | 

 In our view, for a business with one or two clear tasks an external consultant is a smaller step than a hire. If you have enough work for a full position all year, an in-house hire is the right call. If we think you do not need us, we will say so.

 From audit to running system

## Diagnose, build, improve.

 The audit has a fixed scope and timeline agreed up front, and the roadmap points at the number the first build should move.

- 01

### Diagnose

We sit down with the people who do the work and follow one case from the first request to the last step. You get a ranked roadmap, with a clear goal and KPIs for the first build.

- 02

### Build

We build the first item on the roadmap on accounts your business owns. Before it goes live we walk your team through it and hand over written documentation, so they can change it without code.

- 03

### Improve

Once the first item is running we measure it against the agreed number and adjust where the number does not move. If you want to take over, we teach your team to run it.

 Common questions

 Something else on your mind? Write to patrick@mugishamarketing.com.

### What does an AI consultant do?

An AI consultant studies how your business runs, finds the work where AI pays back and says what to build first. At Mugisha AI the consulting comes with the build, so the advice ends up as a working system.

### What is the difference between an AI audit and AI consulting?

The audit is the first step of the consulting. We follow your processes from start to finish and give you a ranked roadmap, with the return to expect at each step. You can act on it with us or on your own.

### How much does AI consulting cost?

It depends on the scope. Each project has a fixed scope and a set timeline, agreed before any work begins, so you know what to expect before you commit.

### Do we need technical people in-house?

No. You need one person who knows how the work runs and can answer our questions. We handle the technical side, from choosing tools to setting them up. What we build fits into the systems you already have, and your team can adjust it without touching code.

### Is our data safe?

We settle this before anything is built. In the audit we map which data a solution would touch and which rules apply to it, such as GDPR and EU hosting. Only then do we choose tools, and everything is set up on accounts your business owns.

### What happens after the roadmap?

You decide. The roadmap works without us: you can hand it to an internal team or another supplier. If you choose us, we build the first item and track the agreed number after launch. If you want to run it yourselves, we show your team how.

# AI Automation for Businesses in Denmark | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/ai-automation/

AI automation

# AI automation that takes routine work off your team.

 AI automation uses software and AI models to carry out repetitive business work on its own, such as sorting incoming requests, updating records and drafting replies. A person still decides which steps get checked before anything goes out. We build it on the tools you already use.

 01, What it is

## Workflows that run themselves.

 AI automation, also called AI workflow automation, is automation in which an AI model reads free text, such as an email, a form or an invoice, and picks the next step instead of following a fixed rule. The rest of the workflow runs as ordinary automation. A person approves the steps you choose.

 Classic automation, often called business process automation, follows fixed rules: when this happens, do that. When a task needs more judgement and several steps, we build AI agents instead. Both are part of our AI agents and automations service.

 Talk to us about this

### The work it removes

Copying details between systems, sorting the inbox, chasing missing information, writing the same reply again and building the weekly report by hand.

### What you get

A working workflow with one clear goal and a number we track from the day it goes live. You choose which steps a person approves. Your team can change the workflow without code, and it runs on accounts your company owns.

### For example

Say supplier invoices arrive by email as PDFs. The workflow reads each one, pulls out the supplier, date and amount, and enters them in your accounting system. When something looks odd, it sends the invoice to a person with a note on what to check. Nobody types the routine ones.

### From a real project

A hotel owner on the Danish coast ran two busy Outlook inboxes. We built an AI email agent in n8n and Microsoft 365 that sorted both inboxes and wrote reply drafts for her to approve. In one week it sorted 121 mails and found the 15 that needed a reply. She told us the drafts were not what she wanted, so we paused them and built what she asked for instead: one mail at 08:00 every morning with the conversations still waiting for her answer.

 02, Tools and fit

## Built on tools you own.

 We pick the tool that fits the job, not the one we like best. Workflows run in n8n, Zapier or Make. Claude and GPT read and write the text. Customer pipelines can live in HighLevel, chat conversations in ManyChat and outreach emails in Instantly. Where your own systems already do the job, we connect to them instead of replacing them. If you are choosing the tool yourself, our guide compares n8n, Make and Zapier. Unsure whether you need RPA or AI? Our guide explains the difference. More reading is in our AI guides.

 Talk to us about this

### Who it is for

Owner-led and mid-size businesses, in Denmark and abroad, where the same steps come round week after week. If you recognise that in your own team, there is probably something to automate. Mugisha AI is an AI automation agency based in Copenhagen.

### How it is set up

Tools are set up on accounts your business owns, so you keep full access. We agree data rules, such as GDPR and EU hosting, before we build.

### Not sure where to start?

Our AI audit ranks your processes and shows what to automate first. For a rollout across several teams, see AI implementation. For customer chat, see AI chatbot for your website.

 03, Which tasks

## Which tasks suit automation?

 Not everything needs AI. Some tasks are best done by a fixed rule, others need a model to read and judge, and some should stay with a person. This is how we sort them.

Task type | Example | Fits | 

Moving data between systems with fixed fields | An order number is copied from the shop to the accounting system. | Fixed automation | 

Sending a message at a set time | A confirmation email the day before a meeting. | Fixed automation | 

Compiling figures for a regular report | Last week’s sales from two systems in one sheet every Monday. | Fixed automation | 

Reading incoming email and sorting it | Questions, complaints and orders land in separate queues. | Needs AI | 

Pulling details out of documents | Supplier, date and amount from an invoice PDF. | Needs AI | 

Writing a first draft of a standard reply | A draft answer to a customer enquiry, approved by a team member. | Needs AI, with approval | 

Negotiating a price or handling an unhappy customer | A call about a late delivery. | Leave to a person | 

Decisions with legal or financial weight | Approving a credit agreement or settling a dispute. | Leave to a person | 

 Many workflows mix the types: a fixed rule moves the data, an AI model reads the email and a person approves whatever looks odd.

### Signs a process is ready to automate

- It repeats often, and each time it follows the same steps.

- Input arrives in a predictable way: the same inbox, the same form, the same file type.

- Someone can write the steps down, including the ones that need judgement, and explain when to choose what.

- You know what a correct result looks like, so it can be checked.

- The systems involved can be connected, or the data can be taken out another way.

- Mistakes are fixable, or a team member can see the result before it reaches a customer.

- Someone on your team owns the process and can answer questions about it.

- You can put a number on it today, such as time, cases or errors, so we can measure whether it improves.

 How we work

## A fixed scope and a clear goal.

 Before any work begins, we agree the scope, the timeline and the number the automation should move.

- 01

### Diagnose

We follow the process from start to finish with the people who do it. We find the step that costs the most time and set a goal and KPIs for it.

- 02

### Build

We build the workflow, test it on real cases and set your approval steps. Before it runs on its own we go through it with your team and hand over written documentation.

- 03

### Improve

After launch we track the agreed number, collect feedback and improve the workflow. If your team will look after it, we show them how to adjust it.

 Common questions

## What people ask about AI automation.

 Something else on your mind? Get in touch and tell us about it.

### What is the difference between automation and AI automation?

Plain automation follows fixed rules and needs tidy, predictable input. AI automation adds a model that can read free text, such as an email or a document, and decide what it means. That lets the workflow handle messy input that rules alone would miss.

### Which tasks are worth automating first?

Start with work that is repeated often, follows a pattern and takes real time, such as entering data, sorting requests or sending follow-ups. We find the best candidates in the diagnose step, and the one with the clearest return goes first.

### Will AI automation replace our people?

The aim is to take routine steps off your team so they have time for work that needs judgement and contact with customers. You decide which steps a person still approves.

### How long does a project take, and what does it cost?

It depends on the scope. Each project has a fixed scope and timeline that we agree before work starts, so you know what to expect. Write to us about your process and we will tell you what fits.

### Is our data safe?

We agree up front which data each workflow uses and where it goes. The tools have to meet your requirements, GDPR and EU hosting for example, and they run on accounts your business owns.

### Can our team change the workflow later?

Yes. We build it so your team can change it without code, and we finish with a documented handover and training. After launch we can keep improving it with you, or leave you to run it.

## Tell us what to automate.

 Write a few lines about the task your team repeats most. Or see all our services.

 Get in touch

# n8n Consultant and n8n Expert | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/n8n-consultant/

n8n consultant

# An n8n consultant for workflows your team can take over.

 An n8n consultant sets up, builds and maintains workflows in n8n so that systems, emails and documents work together without manual copy and paste. They choose where n8n runs, test the workflows, put a person in charge of approving what matters and hand everything over documented, so the company’s own team can take over.

 01, What we build

## n8n workflows that fit your process.

 n8n is a tool that ties systems together in workflows. By its own description you build them visually and can add code where the ready-made steps fall short. 

 Whether you search for an n8n expert, an n8n developer or an n8n agency, these are the kinds of workflow we build in n8n.

 Talk to us about n8n

### Leads and inbox

New enquiries from forms and email land in your CRM and go on to the right person. A model can read an email and sort it as a question, an order or a complaint.

### CRM and documents

Details stay the same across CRM, accounting and spreadsheets, with no double entry. Invoices and other PDFs are read, and supplier, date and amount go into the right system.

### AI agents with approval

An agent can prepare a reply or an action, and a person approves it before anything reaches a customer. n8n itself says you can add human approval where it is needed.

 02, The right tool

## n8n is not always the right choice.

 We have no reason to push one tool. If Make or Zapier suits better, we say so and build there. The full comparison is in our guide n8n vs Make vs Zapier; here is only the rule of thumb. The wider picture is covered under AI automation.

 Talk to us about n8n

### n8n often fits when

Data has to sit in a particular place, the workflow needs its own code, or an internal system has no ready-made connector.

### Make or Zapier often fit when

The person who will adjust the workflow is not technical, or you need to connect many different apps quickly. Then we pick that tool instead.

### Already have an n8n set-up?

We review it first: what runs, on which accounts, and what fails. Then we fix, extend or simplify it, as you choose. Mugisha AI is based in Copenhagen and works with businesses in Denmark and abroad.

 03, Hosting and data

## n8n Cloud or your own server: what suits whom

 n8n can run with n8n itself or on a server you operate. The choice decides who looks after it and where the data sits.

Question | n8n Cloud | Your own server | 

Who runs it | n8n itself, which handles hosting, updates and scaling. | You, on your own infrastructure, on-premises or in a private cloud. | 

Where the data sits | On servers in Frankfurt, Germany. | Wherever you choose to host n8n. | 

Updates and maintenance | Handled by n8n. | Your responsibility: you monitor and update it yourselves. | 

Cost model (our own prices not included) | A subscription based on monthly executions. An execution is one run of the whole workflow, whatever its steps. | The Community Edition is free, but server and running costs come on top. Paid editions need a licence key. | 

Who it suits | Teams without someone to run a server, and where data in Frankfurt is acceptable. | Businesses that want data in their own environment and have someone for the server. The free edition lacks single sign-on and workflow sharing, among other things. | 

 Current plans and prices are on n8n’s own pages, listed under Sources below.

### What has to be in place before we build in n8n

- The process is chosen, and someone on your side owns it.

- The steps can be written down, including those that need judgement.

- You know where data may sit and what data an AI model may see.

- The choice between n8n Cloud and your own server is made, or we make it together.

- If you self-host, someone is responsible for the server and updates.

- Access to the connected systems sits on accounts the company owns.

- You know which steps a person must approve before anything goes to a customer.

- You have a number you can follow from day one: time, cases or errors.

### Sources

 About n8n itself: n8n’s own pages, opened on 20 November 2026.

- n8n homepage: visual builder, code when needed, human approval: https://n8n.io/

- n8n pricing: price per execution, data in Frankfurt, Business self-hosted only: https://n8n.io/pricing/

- n8n guide to choosing Cloud or self-hosting: https://docs.n8n.io/choose-how-to-use-n8n/

- n8n documentation on self-hosting: https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/

- n8n Community Edition features: https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/community-edition-features/

- n8n AI documentation: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google: https://docs.n8n.io/advanced-ai/

- n8n Anthropic Chat Model node: https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/sub-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmchatanthropic/

 How a project runs

## From first call to handover.

 Every project has an agreed scope, timeline and number to measure.

- 01

### Scoping

We go through the process with the people who do it, choose the hosting with you and agree the scope, the timeline and the number to improve.

- 02

### Building

We build the workflow in n8n on accounts you own, test it on real cases and add approval steps where a person should see the result first.

- 03

### Handover

Your team gets the workflows running on your accounts, a written description of each with the systems and access it uses, and a walk-through so you can change them without code.

 Frequently asked questions

## What people ask when they look for an n8n consultant.

 Missing an answer? Write to us and we will help.

### Can you take over an n8n set-up we already have?

Yes. We start by reviewing what runs, on which accounts, and what fails or lacks documentation. Then we agree whether to fix it, build on it or rebuild parts. We need access to your n8n and the systems behind it.

### Do we need a server to use n8n?

Not necessarily. n8n can be hosted by n8n itself, so you do not run a server, or it can run on your own. What suits you depends on where data may sit and whether someone on your side can run a server. See the table above.

### Can n8n use Claude or GPT?

Yes. n8n has a node for Anthropic’s Claude models, and its documentation names OpenAI, behind GPT, and Google as providers. We choose the model for the task and have a person approve what goes to customers.

### Is n8n GDPR-safe?

Hosting alone does not make a workflow GDPR-safe. n8n Cloud stores data in Frankfurt; on your own server it sits where you choose. If a workflow sends text to an AI model, though, it leaves n8n and goes to the model provider. So we agree up front what data each workflow uses.

### Who owns the workflows?

You do. We set n8n up on accounts and servers your company owns, so the workflows and the access sit with you, even if we stop working together.

### Can our team change the workflows afterwards?

Yes. n8n is built visually, and code is only needed where the ready-made steps fall short. We hand over a written description and walk your team through it.

## Tell us what n8n should handle.

 Write a few lines about the process, or the n8n set-up you have today. See also our services.

# AI Agents: AI Agent Development | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/ai-agents/

AI Agents

# AI agents that do the routine work.

 An AI agent is software that takes a task from start to finish. It reads what comes in, decides what it is and carries out the next step in your own systems, such as your email, CRM or shop. We build AI agents for owner-led and mid-size businesses in Denmark and abroad.

 01, What is an AI agent?

## What is an AI agent?

 An AI agent is a program that uses a language model, such as Claude or GPT, to understand a task and carry out its steps in your systems, for example looking up a customer, filling in a record or booking a meeting. It works towards a goal and follows rules for when to stop and ask a person.

 Think of it as a new colleague for one narrow job: you give it the goal and the tools it may use. You may also hear this called agentic AI. What sets it apart from ordinary automation, and when it is the wrong choice, is covered in our guide to agentic AI.

### Automation, chatbot and AI agent side by side

 | What it does | Who decides the steps | Fits when | Main risk | 

Rule-based automation | Runs the same steps every time: if A happens, the system does B. | You, in advance. The steps are written down as rules. | The work does not vary and the input is uniform. | It stalls or gives a wrong result when the input departs from the rules. | 

Chatbot | Answers questions in a conversation from the material it has been given. | The visitor picks the topic. The answer comes from your material. | Many people ask the same questions and an answer is enough. | It answers wrongly or vaguely if the material is incomplete. | 

AI agent | Reads messy input, picks the next step and carries it out in your systems. | The agent chooses within the limits you set. A person approves the steps you name. | The task has several steps and needs some judgement, such as qualifying an enquiry. | It acts wrongly on its own if the limits are too loose, which is why we set rules before it goes live. | 

 02, What it does for you

## The work it takes off your team.

 Most teams lose hours to work that follows a pattern but still needs a little judgement. That is where AI agents fit.

 Talk to us about AI agents

### The work it removes

Sorting the inbox, chasing updates, copying details from one system into another, qualifying leads and answering the same requests every day.

### What you get

A working agent with one clear goal, measured from the day it goes live. You decide which steps a person checks before anything goes out, and your team can change how the agent behaves without code.

### From a real project

A Danish webshop that also sells on Amazon had us build an AI support agent in n8n. It reads each customer email and its photos, picks the compensation from the owner’s own rules and writes the reply. The owner approves, edits or skips before anything is sent. The agent has run since 25 September 2026 and handled 23 customer cases and 35 replies in its first month.

 03, Tools and who it is for

## Built with the tools that fit.

 AI agents are one part of wider AI automation and AI implementation. If you do not know where to start, an AI audit with an AI consultant gives you a prioritised roadmap. Every service is on our services page.

### Tools we build with

We build with n8n, Zapier and Make to connect systems, Claude and GPT to read and write, HighLevel for customer records and pipelines, ManyChat for chat channels and Instantly for email outreach. Choosing between n8n, Make and Zapier? Our guide sets them side by side, and the rest sits in our AI guides.

### Your own systems

Agents work with the systems you already run, such as your email, CRM, calendar or shop. Each connection is set up on accounts your business owns.

### Who it is for

Owner-led and mid-size businesses with roughly 10 to 500 staff, in Denmark and abroad. We have helped 100+ businesses on six continents. Mugisha AI is an AI agent development agency based in Copenhagen.

 04, Rules

## Rules we set before an agent goes live.

 An agent may only do what you have allowed it to do. This has to be in place before it works on real cases:

- One clear goal and one number that shows whether the agent works.

- A list of what it may do on its own and what it must never touch.

- The steps a person approves before anything leaves the building: outgoing email, changes to customer data and anything involving money.

- When it must stop and ask: when it is unsure and when the input looks unusual.

- Which systems and fields it can reach, and nothing beyond that.

- A log of what the agent has done, so a team member can see and correct what happened.

- A test on real cases before it comes near a customer.

- A named person who reviews the results in the first weeks and can switch the agent off.

- Agreed rules for which data it may use and where that data is processed.

 How we build an agent

## Diagnose, build, improve.

 Scope and timeline are fixed before we build. Each agent begins with a bottleneck, a clear goal and the KPIs that show whether it works.

- 01

### Diagnose

We follow the work as it runs today, talk to the people who do it and pick the task where an agent pays off most.

- 02

### Build

We build the agent on accounts you own, test it on real cases and set the rules for when it hands over to a person. Before it goes live we walk your team through it and leave written documentation.

- 03

### Improve

After launch we track the agreed number, collect feedback and improve the agent. If your team will own the agent, we train them to follow it and adjust it.

 Common questions

## What people ask about AI agents.

 Something else on your mind? Write to us.

### What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?

A chatbot answers questions in a conversation. An AI agent also acts: it can update a record, send a draft for approval, book a meeting or pass a case to a person. Many agents have no chat window at all and work in the background on email, forms and your CRM. If you want a chatbot on your website, see our page on an AI chatbot for your website.

### Can an AI agent work with the systems we already use?

Yes, in most cases. We connect agents to your own systems, such as your email, CRM, calendar or shop, with n8n, Zapier or Make. If a system cannot be connected directly, we look at the options in the diagnose step and tell you what is possible before we build.

### Will an AI agent make mistakes?

Sometimes, as people do. That is why we set the rules before launch: which tasks the agent may do alone, which ones a person approves first and when it must stop and ask. We test it on real cases, and after launch we track the agreed number and improve the agent.

### How much does an AI agent cost, and how long does it take?

Both depend on the scope. Each project has a fixed scope and timeline, agreed before work starts, so you know what to expect. The first step is to tell us which task you want off your team’s desk.

### Do we need to hire technical staff for an AI agent?

No. You need one person who knows which task the agent takes over and can approve its first results. We handle the rest of the technical side. Your team can change what we build without code.

### Is our data safe with an AI agent?

We agree up front which data the agent may read and where its output is stored. Tools are picked to match your requirements, such as GDPR and EU hosting, and the agent runs on accounts your business owns. It gets access only to the systems and fields its task needs.

AI implementation

# AI implementation your team will use.

 AI implementation means putting AI to work inside your daily operations. We connect it to your email, records and other systems, set the rules for what it may do, and train the people who use it. You end up with a working system and one agreed number that shows whether it pays off.

 01, What it is

## AI that works inside your daily work.

 AI implementation is the work of taking an AI solution from demo to daily operation: AI integration with your systems, setting rules for what it may do on its own and training the people who use it. It counts as implemented once the work runs through it every day.

 Talk to us about this

### The work it removes

Sorting incoming requests, copying details between systems, writing first drafts of routine replies and preparing reports by hand. These tasks follow the same steps every day, so a system can take them.

### What you get

A working system connected to the tools you already use, with one agreed goal and a number we track from launch. You decide which steps a person approves first. Your team can change it without code, and it runs on accounts your company owns.

### For example

Say a distributor gets orders and questions by email, and one person types each into the order system. We connect the inbox to that system. The AI reads each message, fills in the order and flags anything unclear for a person to check. We agree the goal first, for instance the time from received order to confirmed order.

 02, Tools and fit

## Built with tools you can keep.

 We build with n8n, Zapier and Make for the automations, Claude and GPT for the AI, HighLevel, ManyChat and Instantly where leads and outreach are involved, and your own systems around them. We pick what fits your case.

 Not sure where to start? An AI audit ranks the options first, and you can read about our AI consultant work. See also how we build AI agents and AI automation, or browse all our services.

### Who it is for

A team of about 10 to 500 people, in Denmark or abroad, where the same manual tasks eat hours every week and nobody has time to build the fix. For the national figures on how many Danish companies already use AI, see our facts page. Mugisha AI is based in Copenhagen.

### Your accounts, your data

Tools are set up on accounts your company owns. We agree data rules, such as GDPR and EU hosting, before we start, so you know where your data goes.

### How the deal works

Scope and timeline are fixed before work starts. The project ends with documentation and training, so your team can carry on.

 03, The phases

## The phases of an implementation.

 The table shows what happens in each phase, who on your side needs to spend time, and what you hold when the phase ends. We agree the duration once the scope is known.

Phase | What happens | Who on your side | What you have at the end | 

Mapping | We follow the work as it runs today and choose the task that goes first. | The person who does the work today, and someone who can make decisions. | A description of the task, a goal and the number that should move. | 

Set-up | We create the accounts, connect the systems and set the rules for what the AI may do on its own. | Whoever administers your systems and can grant access. | A solution connected to your systems that does not yet touch real cases. | 

Trial run | We run the solution on real cases with your team alongside and fix what goes wrong. | The team members who will use it. | A test result measured against the agreed goal and a list of fixes. | 

Live running | The solution goes into use and a person approves the steps you agreed. | The team that uses it every day. | A solution in daily use and a handover that describes how it works. | 

Improvement | We follow the number, collect feedback and adjust where it does not move. | Whoever owns the number. | An updated solution and a number that shows whether it pays off. | 

### Why AI projects stall, and what we do about it

- No owner. Nobody on your side is responsible after launch. We agree an owner on your side before we build.

- No number. You cannot see whether it works. We agree one number and measure from day one.

- A first task that is too big. The project tries to change everything at once. We start with one well-defined task.

- The solution does not fit the working day. The team has to open yet another tool. We connect it to the systems you already use.

- No trust in the output. People check everything themselves. We set approval steps and test on real cases with the team.

- Set up on a personal account. It stops working when that person leaves. We build on accounts your company owns.

- No follow-up. The solution quietly goes out of date. We track the number after launch and make fixes, and your team can change it without code.

 How an implementation runs

## A clear goal before we build.

 Before we build anything, it is fixed what the project covers, when it is done and which number has to move to show it works.

- 01

### Diagnose

We start with the people who do the work and trace each process end to end. We find the bottleneck, set a clear goal and agree the KPIs before we build anything.

- 02

### Build

We connect the tools, set the rules for what the AI may do alone and what a person checks, and test it with your team. The handover comes with written documentation and training for the people who will use it.

- 03

### Improve

After launch we track the agreed number, collect feedback and make improvements. If your team takes over the running, the training is part of the project.

AI chatbot

# An AI chatbot for your website that answers like your team.

 An AI chatbot for your website answers visitors’ questions in plain language, using your own prices, policies and product information. It can also take down details, book a meeting and pass the conversation to a person when it should. We build it, connect it to your systems and keep improving it after launch.

 01, What it is

## A chatbot that knows your business.

 An AI chatbot for a website, or website chatbot, is a chat window that reads visitors’ questions as they are written and answers from the material you give it: your FAQ, prices, product pages and policies. If it does not know the answer, it says so and hands the conversation to your team.

 Older chatbots follow a fixed menu: pick an option, get a canned reply. An AI chatbot reads the question as it is written and can answer wordings it has not seen before.

 Talk to us about this

### The work it removes

The same customer service questions arriving by email, phone and chat: opening hours, delivery, what is included and how to book. It also takes the first round of back and forth with new leads, so your team starts the conversation further along. When the job goes beyond answering, the chatbot can be the front of an AI agent that acts on the request.

### What you get

A chatbot on your website, built on your own information and set up to match your tone. It collects the details your team needs, books meetings in your calendar and hands over to a person with the whole conversation attached. You decide which topics it handles and which it never touches.

### For example

Say a company that installs heat pumps gets the same questions about timing, how long an installation takes and what a visit involves. The chatbot answers from the company’s own material. A visitor who wants a quote leaves an address and a phone number, and the chatbot books a call. The salesperson can read the conversation before dialling.

 02, Tools and fit

## Built with tools you can see.

 We choose the language model and the chat tool that suit your setup, and connect them to the systems your team already uses.

 Talk to us about this

### Tools we build with

Claude or GPT reads the question and writes the answer. n8n, Zapier or Make connect the chat to your systems. HighLevel handles contacts and bookings, and ManyChat covers chat on social channels. We also work with your own systems, such as your CRM, helpdesk or booking tool.

### Who it is for

Owner-led and mid-size businesses, from about 10 to 500 staff, in Denmark and abroad. It fits best where customers ask many of the same questions and a few people spend part of every day answering them. Not sure a chatbot is the right first step? An AI audit, part of our AI consulting, ranks what to build first. Mugisha AI is based in Copenhagen.

### Your accounts, your data

The chatbot lives on accounts your business owns. Before launch we agree which data it may use and where conversations are stored, including GDPR and EU hosting. See all our services, or read about AI automation if you want more than a chatbot.

 03, Before launch

## What the chatbot needs from you.

 How a chatbot differs from plain automation and from an AI agent is set out in the comparison table on our AI agents page. Below is what the chatbot needs from you before it goes live.

### What we need from you before the chatbot goes live

- Your FAQ, prices, delivery terms and product information as text we may use.

- A decision on which topics it may handle and which it must never touch, such as complaints or legal questions.

- Hand-over rules: when it passes a conversation to a person, to whom and on which channel.

- Your opening hours and what happens outside them, for example the chatbot takes the enquiry and your team answers next morning.

- The languages it should answer in.

- Access to your calendar, CRM or helpdesk, if it should book meetings or open cases.

- A short notice for visitors that they are writing with an AI and how the conversation is stored, agreed with your privacy policy.

- A person who can update the answers when prices or terms change.

- The number it should move, such as questions answered without your team or meetings booked.

# What Is Agentic AI? A Plain Guide | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/guides/what-is-agentic-ai/

# What is agentic AI?

Last updated: 21 November 2026 · Reviewed by Patrick Mugisha, founder

Agentic AI is software that works towards a goal on its own. It plans the steps, uses tools such as email, a calendar or a CRM, checks what happened and adjusts, and it stops to ask a person when a rule says so. A chatbot answers questions; an agentic system carries out tasks.

## How agentic AI differs from what you already know

Four things often get mixed up. The table shows how they differ in practice.

 | Chatbot | Fixed automation | Single AI agent | Agentic AI system | 

What it does | Answers questions in a conversation | Runs the same steps every time something happens | Handles one task and picks its own steps | One or more agents, with rules and checkpoints, working towards a goal across several systems | 

Who chooses the steps | You, one question at a time | Whoever built it, in advance | The AI model, within limits you set | The AI models, within limits and checkpoints you set | 

Touches your systems | Rarely | Yes, exactly as built | Yes, the tools it is given | Yes, through several tools, with a log and approvals | 

Example | Website chat that answers opening hours | A form creates a CRM record and sends a confirmation | Reads a new enquiry, finds the customer and drafts a reply | Follows an enquiry from first message to booked meeting, and asks a person before anything reaches a customer | 

Main risk | A wrong or invented answer | Stops when the input looks different from what was expected | Takes a wrong step on its own | More parts to keep an eye on | 

Anthropic’s guide Building effective agents draws the line like this: workflows are “systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths”, while agents are “systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage”. OpenAI’s agents guide says agents “can plan and complete tasks using tools, work with other agents, and maintain context across steps”.

Because of this, “agent” and “agentic” are used loosely. In this guide, “agentic AI” means the whole approach and “agent” means one part of it. That is how we use the words, not an official definition.

## Examples for a company with 10 to 500 staff

These are illustrations of the kind of task that fits, not results from a client.

### Handling new enquiries

The agent reads an enquiry from the website form or an inbox, checks the CRM to see whether the customer already exists, drafts a reply and suggests a time for a call. A person approves the reply before anything is sent.

### Sorting incoming mail

The agent reads messages from customers and suppliers, finds the order or invoice number, matches it with the accounting system and flags anything that does not match. A person handles the exceptions.

### Following up on quotes

The agent finds quotes that have had no answer after a set number of days, drafts a reminder that fits the quote and puts it in a queue for the salesperson to send or change.

### Moving data between systems

When a deal is won, the agent checks that the customer record is complete, creates the customer and project in the other system and lists what is missing for a person to fill in.

## What it takes to run one safely

- A person approves what leaves the company. Anthropic notes that agents can “pause for human feedback at checkpoints or when encountering blockers”. We start with the agent drafting and a person sending.

- Limits. Decide which tools and data the agent may reach and how many steps it may take. Anthropic recommends including “stopping conditions (such as a maximum number of iterations) to maintain control”.

- A log. Every step the agent takes is recorded, so you can see what happened and why, and fix it when something goes wrong.

- Testing before use. Anthropic recommends “extensive testing in sandboxed environments, along with the appropriate guardrails”. We run an agent on test data before it touches live customers.

- EU rules. The European Commission says the AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and became applicable on 2 August 2026, with some exceptions. It says people should be made aware when they interact with a machine, and it lists “appropriate human oversight measures” as a requirement for high-risk systems. Whether a use is high-risk is a legal question, so ask your adviser about anything that affects decisions about people.

- Personal data. If the agent handles personal data, agree where the data is processed and who the processor is before the first run, as you would for any GDPR-covered tool.

## When not to use agentic AI

Anthropic recommends “finding the simplest solution possible, and only increasing complexity when needed”, and notes that “agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance”. In practice, skip it when:

- the steps are always the same, because ordinary automation is simpler and easier to check;

- a mistake is costly and cannot be undone, such as a payment or a contract;

- nobody in the company will own the result and read the log;

- the data lives in places nobody can reach, because an agent cannot work with what it cannot see.

## How to start

- Pick one narrow task that a named person does today and finds tedious.

- Write down the steps as that person does them, and what a good result looks like.

- Let the agent suggest, and let the person decide, for the first weeks.

- Compare its suggestions with what the person would have done, and adjust the rules.

- Widen the agent’s freedom only where the log shows it has been right.

When you are ready to build one, see our AI agents service. If you are not sure which task to start with, our AI consultant service begins with exactly that question.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is agentic AI in simple terms?

It is AI that carries out a task instead of only answering a question. It plans the steps, uses your tools, checks the result and asks a person when a rule says it should. Think of a new colleague with one narrow job and clear limits.

### What is the difference between an AI agent and agentic AI?

An AI agent is one piece of software that handles a task. Agentic AI is the wider approach, where one or more agents work towards a goal with rules, approvals and logs around them. The words are used loosely, so check what a vendor means.

### Is agentic AI the same as a chatbot?

No. A chatbot talks with you and answers. An agentic system also acts: it can read an enquiry, look up a customer, update a record or draft a message. That is why it needs limits and approval steps that a simple chatbot does not.

### Is agentic AI safe for a business to use?

It can be used responsibly, but it is not safe by default. Give it a narrow task, limit the tools and data it can reach, keep a log of every step and let a person approve anything that leaves the company. Start with suggestions before actions.

### Does the EU AI Act apply to agentic AI?

The European Commission’s page says the AI Act became applicable on 2 August 2026, with some exceptions, and that it sorts AI systems by risk. Which level an agent falls into depends on what it does. We cannot give legal advice, so ask your adviser about anything that affects people.

### Do we need agentic AI, or is ordinary automation enough?

If the steps are always the same, ordinary automation is simpler, cheaper to run and easier to check. Agentic AI is worth considering when the input varies and a person now spends time reading, sorting and deciding what to do next.

More plain guides are in our AI guides, or contact us with the task you have in mind.

Tell us the task you want off your team’s desk. We will tell you whether an agent fits or whether plain automation is enough.

# n8n vs Make vs Zapier: Which Fits Your Team | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/guides/n8n-vs-make-vs-zapier/

# n8n vs Make vs Zapier: which one fits your business?

Last updated: 21 November 2026 · Reviewed by Patrick Mugisha, founder

Choose Zapier if the number of apps you can connect matters most, because it lists more than 9,000 of them. Choose Make if you want a visual canvas for workflows with branches and steps that depend on each other. Choose n8n if you want to host the tool yourself, keep data on your own servers or add code where the standard steps stop. All three can run AI steps, so the choice comes down to hosting, pricing model and who will look after the workflows.

## What each tool is

### n8n

n8n calls itself the platform for agents and workflows you can follow. It lists more than 500 native integrations and can reach any service with an API through an HTTP step. You can use the version n8n hosts for you or install it on your own server. The source code is on GitHub, and a free Community Edition exists for self-hosting. It includes almost the complete feature set, but leaves out things such as single sign-on, sharing of workflows and Git version control, which sit in the paid editions.

### Make

Make describes itself as an AI automation platform for building workflows and AI agents visually. You build by dragging modules onto a canvas, or by prompting. It lists more than 3,000 native apps, and any service with a public API can be connected through a custom app. Its page says Make is GDPR compliant and holds SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 certification.

### Zapier

Zapier describes itself as the control plane that connects any AI to any tool. It lists more than 9,000 apps and says more than 3 million businesses use it. You build automations, called Zaps, from a trigger and one or more actions. It also lists GDPR compliance next to its SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 reports.

## Side by side

 | n8n | Make | Zapier | 

Hosting | Hosted by n8n, or self-hosted on your own server | Make’s cloud. We found no self-hosted option on the pages we read | Zapier’s cloud. We found no self-hosted option on the pages we read | 

Pricing model | Per workflow execution, however many steps it has. Hosted plans start at €20 a month billed annually, for 2,500 executions | Per credit. Most actions use 1 credit, routers use none. The free plan has 1,000 credits a month. Paid prices were not shown on the page we read | Per task, meaning a successfully completed action. Triggers and built-in tools such as Filter do not count. Free has 100 tasks, Professional starts at $19.99 a month billed annually for 750 tasks | 

AI features | AI Agent node, MCP client and server trigger, human approval for tool calls | AI agents, the Maia assistant, an MCP server, AI apps. Some AI features use more credits | Zapier Agents, Copilot (beta), AI by Zapier on paid plans, Zapier MCP | 

Coding needed | Not for basic workflows. Code can be added where you need it | No. You build on a canvas, by drag and drop or by prompting | No for standard steps. A Code by Zapier step is available | 

EU data and self-hosting | Hosted plans keep data in Frankfurt, Germany. Self-hosted data sits wherever you host it | Make: “Your Data zone is the Make setting on your organization (US1, US2, EU1, EU2).” But “Selecting the EU1 or EU2 data zone does not automatically mean every request gets processed and stays in the EU.” Make lists GDPR compliance | No data region stated on the pages we read. Zapier lists GDPR compliance | 

Best for | Teams that want control over hosting and data, or need custom code | Workflows with branches and many steps, built visually | Linking many different apps quickly, and the widest app list | 

The table is a summary. Prices and plan names change, so check the vendor pages in the sources list before you decide.

## When to choose each

### Choose n8n when

- Your data rules say the tool must run on servers you control, or in a named place.

- You expect to write some custom code or call internal systems that have no ready-made connector.

- You are happy to pay by workflow run rather than by step.

- Someone on your side, or a partner, can look after a server if you self-host.

### Choose Make when

- The workflow branches, loops or has many steps, and you want to see the whole flow on one canvas.

- The person who will adjust it is an operations lead, not a developer.

- You want to build AI agents and ordinary workflows in the same place.

### Choose Zapier when

- You need to connect many different apps, including less common ones.

- The jobs are short and linear: when this happens, do that.

- You want a hosted tool with nothing to install and a free plan to try it on.

If none of these fits clearly, the systems you already use usually decide it. Check which tool has a ready-made connector for your CRM, your accounting system and your email, because a missing connector costs more time than any price gap.

## What it costs in practice

The monthly price matters less than the billing unit, because the three tools count work differently.

- n8n counts executions. One run of a workflow is one execution, whether it has three steps or thirty.

- Make counts credits. Most actions use one credit, and routers and error handlers use none. When credits run out, scenarios stop.

- Zapier counts tasks. A task is a successfully completed action. Triggers, filters, formatting and other built-in tools do not count, and failed actions are not charged.

Here is a worked example, not a client result. A workflow has one trigger and four actions and runs 1,000 times a month. In n8n that is 1,000 executions, which fits inside the 2,500 on the Starter plan. In Zapier it is up to 4,000 tasks, because the trigger does not count, which is well above the 750-task entry tier of Professional. In Make it is a few thousand credits, since most actions use one credit. The same job can be cheapest in a different tool depending on how many steps it has and how often it runs.

Three costs sit outside the plan price. If you self-host n8n, you pay for a server and someone to keep it updated and backed up. AI steps can bring a model bill from the provider, unless the plan includes the models. Building also takes time: a workflow that nobody documents becomes expensive the first time its author is away.

## Common mistakes

- Choosing by price alone, without counting how many steps the workflow has and how often it runs.

- Picking the tool before looking at which systems it has to connect to.

- Building on a personal account. When that person leaves, the workflows stop or get locked.

- Letting an AI step send messages to customers with no person checking the first weeks of output.

- Skipping error alerts, so a broken workflow stays silent for days.

- Building one huge workflow instead of small ones that each do one job.

- Settling the data question after the build. Where data is processed should be agreed before the first workflow.

## How we work with these tools

We build with all three, and we have no reason to push one of them. For n8n on its own, see n8n consultant. We pick the tool that fits your systems and your team, and we tell you why. Every project starts with a bottleneck, a clear goal and the number it should move. Scope and timeline are fixed before work starts.

We set the tools up on accounts you own, so you keep the workflows if we part ways. The data rules, such as GDPR and where data is hosted, are agreed up front. We finish with a documented handover and training, and we build so your team can change what we made without writing code.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is n8n free?

The Community Edition is free to self-host, and its code is on GitHub. The hosted plans are paid and start at €20 a month billed annually, for 2,500 executions. Self-hosting is free of licence fees but not free of work: you need a server and someone to maintain it.

### Is Make cheaper than Zapier?

It depends on the workflow, and we cannot quote a Make price because the pricing page we read showed no figures for its paid plans. Make has a free plan with 1,000 credits a month, and Zapier’s free plan has 100 tasks. Because a credit and a task are counted differently, compare the two by running your real workflow through each pricing calculator.

### Which tool keeps data in the EU?

n8n’s hosted plans store data in Frankfurt, Germany, and a self-hosted n8n keeps data wherever you host it. Make states: “Your Data zone is the Make setting on your organization (US1, US2, EU1, EU2).” It also states: “Selecting the EU1 or EU2 data zone does not automatically mean every request gets processed and stays in the EU.” The Zapier pages we read list GDPR compliance but do not name a data region. If region matters to you, ask the vendor in writing before you build.

### Can I switch tools later?

Yes, but workflows do not copy from one tool to another. You rebuild them. The documentation, the logic and the list of systems carry over, which is why we document every workflow we build.

### Do I need a developer to use these tools?

Not for ordinary workflows. All three can be used without writing code. A developer helps when you self-host n8n, when you call systems that have no connector, or when a workflow becomes large and needs tidy structure.

### Can these tools run AI agents?

Yes. n8n has an AI Agent node with human approval for tool calls, Make has AI agents, and Zapier has Zapier Agents. An agent still needs a clear task, limits on what it may do and a person who checks the output.

Read more about AI automation and AI agents, or contact us with the process you want to automate. More plain guides are in our AI guides, such as what agentic AI is.

# RPA vs AI Automation: What Is the Difference? | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/guides/rpa-vs-ai-automation/

# RPA vs AI automation: what is the difference?

Last updated: 21 November 2026 · Reviewed by Patrick Mugisha, founder

RPA repeats fixed clicks and keystrokes on screens, so it works while the input and the screens stay the same. AI automation uses a language model to read and judge messy input such as emails and documents, and a workflow then acts on the result. Most real jobs use both: rules for the steps, AI for the reading.

## The four kinds side by side

“Automation” covers four different things. The table is our summary of how they differ in practice.

 | RPA | Workflow automation (n8n, Make, Zapier) | AI automation | AI agent | 

How it works | A software robot repeats recorded actions on screens | Steps connected through the apps’ own interfaces, in a fixed order | A workflow with one or more steps where an AI model reads, sorts or drafts | A model chooses which tools to use and in what order, within limits | 

Input it handles | Structured, the same layout every time | Structured data from apps, forms and files | Free text, documents and mixed formats | Open-ended tasks with varying input | 

What breaks it | A moved button, a new screen layout, a pop-up | A changed field or a changed app interface | A wrong reading of unusual input | A wrong step taken on its own | 

Typical use | Moving data in a system with no other way in | Form to CRM, order to invoice, notifications | Sorting mail, reading invoices, drafting replies | Looking things up across systems and proposing next steps | 

## What the vendors say

UiPath, a large RPA vendor, writes that “Robotic process automation (RPA) uses software robots to automate repetitive, rule-based tasks like data entry and system integration.” Microsoft describes its desktop flows for “simple or complex rule-based tasks on their workstations” and says you can interact with the machine “by using application UI elements, images, or coordinates”.

IBM draws the line against AI: “The critical difference is that RPA is process-driven, whereas AI is data-driven.” It adds that “RPA bots can follow only the processes defined by an end user, while AI bots use machine learning to recognize patterns in data, in particular unstructured data, and learn over time.”

For the last column, n8n’s documentation says that “the agent decides which tools to call to complete a task”. Anthropic separates workflows, “systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths”, from agents, “systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage”. Our guide to agentic AI goes further into the agent side.

## Four tasks, four answers

These are illustrations of how we would sort tasks, not client results.

### A supplier portal with no other way in

Staff copy invoice lines from a portal into the accounting system. The portal has no integration and its pages look the same every time. That is RPA territory. If the portal offers an interface for data, a workflow is steadier.

### A form that must create a record

A website form should create a CRM contact and send a confirmation. The input is structured and the steps never change. A plain workflow in n8n, Make or Zapier does this, with no AI. Our comparison of n8n, Make and Zapier helps you choose.

### Customer emails in free text

Emails arrive about orders, delays and returns, each worded differently. A model reads each one and picks out the topic and the order number. A workflow files it, and a person approves anything that goes to a customer. That is AI automation.

### A query that needs several lookups

A supplier asks why a delivery is late. Answering means checking the order system, the shipping notice and earlier mail, then choosing what to do. That fits an agent with narrow tools and a log, started in suggestion mode.

## How to combine them

In our experience the strongest setups use each kind where it is cheapest and most predictable. A workflow forms the backbone and moves data between apps. An AI step handles the reading of messy input. An RPA step is used only where an app has no other door. An agent is reserved for the part that really varies, with a person approving what leaves the company. Anthropic’s advice applies: “we recommend finding the simplest solution possible, and only increasing complexity when needed”.

Our pages on AI automation, n8n and AI agents describe what we build in each case.

## Three questions to sort a task

Ask these in order. They are our own rule of thumb.

- Does the app offer an interface for its data? If so, use a workflow. If the screen is the only way in, RPA is a candidate.

- Is the input always the same shape? If it is free text or documents, add an AI step to read it.

- Does the next step depend on what was found? If the path is not known in advance, consider an agent, with limits and approval.

## Keep the RPA robot or replace it?

This is our view, not a rule. Keep a robot when it runs steadily, the screens rarely change, the input is structured and someone knows how it works. Replacing it will cost more than it saves.

Consider replacing it when:

- it stops every time the screen layout changes and fixing it takes more time than the task;

- the input has become free text that the robot cannot read;

- the application now offers an interface for data, so screens are no longer needed;

- nobody can say how it works or who owns it.

Even then, replace it one task at a time and run the old and new side by side before switching off the robot.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the difference between RPA and AI automation?

RPA repeats fixed actions on screens and needs the same input each time. AI automation adds a model that can read and judge varying input, such as an email. In most projects the two are combined with a workflow tool.

### Is RPA the same as workflow automation?

No. RPA works on the screen like a person would. Workflow tools such as n8n, Make and Zapier connect apps through their own interfaces. Where an app offers one, a workflow is usually the steadier choice.

### Is an AI agent better than RPA?

Not by default. An agent can handle varied input but chooses its own steps, so it needs limits, logs and approval. For a fixed task with stable screens, RPA or a plain workflow is simpler and easier to check.

### Can AI replace our RPA robots?

Sometimes, in part. Where a robot fails because the input varies, an AI step can take over that reading. Robots that run steadily on fixed screens can stay. Replace them one task at a time.

### Do we need RPA if we use n8n, Make or Zapier?

Often not. If the apps have interfaces, workflow tools reach them directly. RPA is mainly useful where an application can only be used through its screen.

### Where do we start if we are unsure which fits?

Write down one task, its input and how often the input changes. Fixed input points to a workflow or RPA. Free text points to AI automation. Tell us the task and we will say which fits.

More plain guides are in our AI guides, or contact us with the task you have in mind.

# What Is an AI Audit? A Plain Guide | Mugisha AI
URL: https://mugishamarketing.com/guides/what-is-an-ai-audit/

# What is an AI audit?

Last updated: 21 November 2026 · Reviewed by Patrick Mugisha, founder

An AI audit is a structured review of how your business actually works, carried out to find which tasks AI can take over and which it should not. It ends in a ranked roadmap: what to build first, what to leave alone and what each item should change. The same word is sometimes used for testing an AI system itself.

## What an audit looks at

A good audit starts with the work, not with a tool. The reviewer follows real cases through the business and looks at five things.

- Volume and rhythm. What repeats, how often and how many hours it takes.

- How information moves. Where it enters, who retypes it and where it gets stuck between systems.

- Rules or judgement. Which steps follow a fixed rule and which need a person to weigh something up.

- Conditions. The data involved, the rules that apply to it and where it may be stored.

- Ownership. Who owns each task today, who will own the result and what number should improve.

## What you get at the end

The main deliverable is a ranked roadmap. Each item names the task, the reason it sits where it does, what it needs (access, data, a person with time), the number it should move and what could go wrong. Ranking is a judgement. In our view it should weigh hours saved, risk and effort together, and it should say plainly what is not worth building.

Sometimes the best item is not AI at all. Anthropic, in its guide to building agents, recommends “finding the simplest solution possible, and only increasing complexity when needed”. An audit that sends every task to AI has not done its job.

## AI audit, AI strategy, AI workshop or readiness assessment

The four terms overlap and vendors use them loosely. The table is our reading of how they are usually meant, not an official definition.

 | What it is | What you get | When it fits | 

AI audit | A review of real work and systems, case by case | A ranked roadmap with a number to move for each item | You have repeated tasks and want to know what to build first | 

AI strategy | A direction for the whole business over a longer period | A document on goals, priorities and principles | Leadership must agree where AI belongs before any project | 

AI workshop | A shared working session with your people | Common understanding and a list of ideas | The team needs a shared picture, or ideas must be collected | 

AI readiness assessment | A check of data, systems, skills and governance | A score or gap list against a chosen yardstick | You suspect data or access may block you before you start | 

## How to prepare

You can make an audit faster and cheaper to run by arriving with a few things in hand:

- Name the person who knows how the work runs and can answer questions during the week.

- Pick two or three tasks that annoy people most, even if you are unsure AI fits.

- Gather examples of real inputs: a handful of recent emails, orders or forms, with personal details removed where you can.

- List the systems in use and who holds the logins.

- Write down one number you wish would improve, such as days to answer a customer.

- Decide who may say yes to a first build once the roadmap arrives.

## How to judge an audit report

These are our own rules of thumb, not a standard.

### Signs of a good report

- It names the cases it followed and shows the steps it saw.

- Every item has an owner, a number to move and a reason for its rank.

- It says what not to build and what to fix without AI.

- Assumptions and gaps are written down as assumptions and gaps.

- You could hand it to another supplier or your own team and they could act on it.

### Signs of a weak report

- It is a tool list with no connection to your tasks.

- Gains are given as bold figures with no way to check them.

- Everything it proposes happens to need one product or one supplier.

- It skips data, access and who is responsible when something goes wrong.

## If you already use AI

Some audits also look at AI systems you already run. The US standards institute NIST says it “has developed a framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence (AI)”, released on 26 January 2023 and “intended for voluntary use”. It is one yardstick an audit can use for risk. It is not a certificate, and we do not claim that following it makes a system compliant with any law.

## What to do afterwards

- Choose the first roadmap item that is small, frequent and has a named owner.

- Write down what a good result looks like and how you will measure it from the first day.

- Let the system suggest and a person decide for the first weeks.

- Compare its work with what the person would have done, then adjust.

- Return to the roadmap and decide on the next item only when the first one has shown its number.

If you want a supplier to run the audit and build the first item, our AI consultant page explains how our audit works and what we need from you. For what an agent can take on, read what is agentic AI.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an AI audit in simple terms?

It is a review of how your business works that ends in a ranked list of what AI could take over, what it should not and what to build first. It starts with your tasks and data, not with a product.

### How is an AI audit different from an AI strategy?

An audit is concrete: it follows real work and produces a ranked list of items to build. A strategy is broader and sets direction and principles. A strategy without an audit can stay abstract, and an audit without a strategy can miss the bigger picture.

### Is an AI audit the same as an AI readiness assessment?

Not quite. A readiness assessment checks whether your data, systems and skills are ready for AI, usually against a yardstick. An audit asks which work to hand over and in what order. The two can be done together.

### Who should take part in an AI audit?

The people who do the work, one person who can answer questions about systems and data, and a decision maker who can approve a first build. Without the people who do the work, the audit only sees the official process.

### What should an AI audit report contain?

The cases followed, a ranked list of items, the number each should move, what each needs and what could go wrong. It should also list what is not worth building and which assumptions it could not check.

### Do we have to build with the same company that audited?

No. A good roadmap works without its author. You can hand it to your own team or another supplier. If you choose us, we build the first item and follow the agreed number after launch.

More plain guides are in our AI guides, or contact us with the task you have in mind.

- What is agentic AI?

- n8n vs Make vs Zapier

- RPA vs AI automation

- AI in Danish businesses: figures and sources 2026

## Sources

- Anthropic, Building effective agents (19 December 2024): https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents

Tell us which tasks eat your team’s week. We will say whether an audit is the right first step.
